habitat: Rocky areas in dry to mesic savanna. SABAP1 says it is partially arboreal and occurs singly or in pairs.
summary: No Newman page. Wikipedia describes a large pipit with yellow-green edges to the wing coverts and olive-brown underparts streaked dark brown. The song is loud, penetrating and thrush-like, from a rock or perch. SABAP1 says the wing and tail feathers are edged lemon-yellow, and that territorial males sing a loud, almost canary-like song in the breeding season. Neither source states residency, so status and months are unset. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

underparts.pattern: Olive-brown with dark brown streaking. Olive-brown is not a colour token.

wings.pattern: Wikipedia: yellow-green edges to the wing coverts. SABAP1: wing and tail feathers edged lemon-yellow.

tail.shape: SABAP1 says the tail feathers are edged lemon-yellow.

viewNotes.note: Streaked olive-brown underparts. The upperpart colour was not described apart from the wing edges.
Dark brown streaking on the underparts.
Wing coverts edged yellow-green, or lemon-yellow in the SABAP1 wording.
A flight pattern was not described. The yellow edges may show on the open wing.
Olive-brown underparts with dark brown streaks.
